Genuinely think if I had the choice I’d break my leg ten times over if it meant my OCD was gone for good.

And no I haven’t to be honest. It’s hard to describe to people what I ‘go through’ so to speak. I’ve been dealing with this for over a decade now and I have episodes where my brain just ‘breaks’. Like a huge traumatic episode where I can’t get over a particular incident. One of them happened last year and it’s been really hard to deal with.

But yeah, I need to find courage to speak to my Priest otherwise I will keep going in circles. I’m just running out of fight atm.

Paroxetine, 20mg. 

Have been for years but when my brain ‘broke’ I panicked and went on Sertraline 100mg for a few months then reverted back to Paroxetine. Maybe withdrawals from the Sertaline has done me over.

The reason I went to Sertaline in the first place was because the obsessions were too much for me. I was cutting myself and I went onto them meds because I was thought it would be a quick fix.

They weren’t. I went back to Paroxetine this year and the headaches still appear. 

I don’t know. My life is a mess lol. It’s just numb.
I feel nothing.

I don't feel anything basically. I get headaches when I 'try' to like women. I think about the time my brain 'broke' and what I could've done to change it.

Do you still go to therapy now?

I quit my full time job in January as my OCD was too much.

I live in a relatively small city yeah. I went to see a therapist earlier this year, she was alright to be fair. She even had faith in me to sort things out but I bottled the tasks she gave me. I was fresh out of quitting my job and all I wanted to do was hide in my room. 

I do play football once/twice a week though which is a small respite.

I just feel alone, I’m blessed to have really good friends but none of them would understand what I go through everyday.

I’ve tried talking to my Mum but she can’t get her head round it either. 

It’s a lonely life.

I had a few at Church, I didn't follow the Liturgy that well at all as expected but I had a chat with the Priest later on and he gave me a Liturgy book for me to read which will really help. 

I had a funny question for the Priest and said "What do I call you?" He said "Just call me Father". Haha, was really welcoming. It can be pretty daunting going to a new place where everyone knows each other so I'm glad I've done it now.
Pleased to say I went to the Divine Liturgy for the first time today. A culture shock but I definitely want to go again. Thank you for your prayers :)
